subject: Physics
topic: 1D and 2D Relative Velocity, River-Swimmer, Rain-Man Problems

questions.sourceLocator: Section 3.6, Page 51 (Relative Velocity in One Dimension)
questions.stem: Two trains A and B of lengths 100 m and 150 m are moving on parallel tracks in opposite directions with speeds 36 km/h and 54 km/h respectively. The time taken by them to completely cross each other is:
questions.solution: Relative distance to cover = L_A + L_B = 100 + 150 = 250 m. Relative velocity v_rel = v_A + v_B = 36 km/h + 54 km/h = 90 km/h = 90 * (5/18) = 25 m/s. Time t = 250 / 25 = 10 s.
questions.aiCritique: Standard NCERT 1D relative motion problem verified.

secondPassQA.notes: Conceptually rigorous, single-choice unambiguous, units verified.

questions.sourceLocator: Section 4.9, Page 77 (Relative Velocity in Two Dimensions)
questions.stem: Rain is falling vertically downwards with a speed of 35 m/s. A woman rides a bicycle with a speed of 12 m/s in east to west direction. The direction in which she should hold her umbrella is:
questions.solution: v_rain = -35 ĵ, v_cyclist = -12 î. Relative velocity of rain with respect to woman v_rw = v_rain - v_cyclist = 12 î - 35 ĵ. To protect from rain, umbrella is held opposite to v_rw, i.e. in direction -12 î + 35 ĵ (tilted towards west). tan θ = |v_w| / |v_r| = 12/35 with vertical towards west.
questions.aiCritique: Rain-cyclist vector angle directly aligned with NCERT Example 4.6.

secondPassQA.notes: Conceptually rigorous, single-choice unambiguous, units verified.

questions.sourceLocator: NCERT Class 11 Exercise & Exemplar Concept Equivalent (Ch 03)
questions.stem: A swimmer can swim with a speed of 5 km/h in still water. He crosses a 1 km wide river flowing at 3 km/h along the shortest possible path. The time taken by him is:
questions.solution: For shortest path (direct crossing across the river), net velocity along perpendicular is v_net = √(v_s² - v_r²) = √(5² - 3²) = √16 = 4 km/h. Time t = d / v_net = 1 km / 4 km/h = 1/4 hour = 15 minutes.

secondPassQA.notes: Conceptually rigorous, single-choice unambiguous, units verified.

questions.sourceLocator: NCERT Class 11 Exercise & Exemplar Concept Equivalent (Ch 03)
questions.stem: A man crosses a 500 m wide river flowing at 4 km/h in the shortest possible time. If his speed in still water is 5 km/h, the drift of the man along the river bank upon reaching the opposite side is (in meters):
questions.solution: For shortest time, swimmer heads directly perpendicular to flow. Time t = width / v_s = 0.5 km / 5 km/h = 0.1 hour = 6 minutes. Drift x = v_river * t = 4 km/h * 0.1 hour = 0.4 km = 400 meters.
questions.aiCritique: Shortest time drift calculation checked with exact integer result.

secondPassQA.notes: Conceptually rigorous, single-choice unambiguous, units verified.

questions.sourceLocator: NCERT Class 11 Exercise & Exemplar Concept Equivalent (Ch 03)
questions.stem: Ship A is moving Westwards with a speed of 10 km/h and ship B, 100 km South of A, is moving Northwards with a speed of 10 km/h. The time after which the distance between them becomes shortest is:
questions.solution: Let A be at origin initially, B at (0, -100). At time t, position of A: r_A = -10t î. Position of B: r_B = (-100 + 10t) ĵ. Distance squared S² = (-10t)² + (10t - 100)² = 100t² + 100t² - 2000t + 10000 = 200t² - 2000t + 10000. For minimum distance: d(S²)/dt = 400t - 2000 = 0 => t = 5 hours.
questions.aiCritique: Classic shortest approach calculus optimization verified.

secondPassQA.notes: Conceptually rigorous, single-choice unambiguous, units verified.

questions.stem: Two particles A and B are dropped from heights h₁ and h₂ simultaneously from rest. The relative acceleration of particle A with respect to particle B during free fall is:
questions.solution: Both particles experience downward gravitational acceleration a_A = -g and a_B = -g. Relative acceleration a_AB = a_A - a_B = (-g) - (-g) = 0.
questions.aiCritique: Zero relative acceleration in uniform gravitational field verified.

secondPassQA.notes: Conceptually rigorous, single-choice unambiguous, units verified.

questions.sourceLocator: NCERT Class 11 Exercise & Exemplar Concept Equivalent (Ch 03)
questions.stem: Two bodies A and B are thrown simultaneously from two points separated by 100 m on the ground with equal speed u = 20 m/s towards each other at angles 30° and 60° to horizontal. The time in seconds when they collide is:
questions.solution: Relative horizontal velocity v_rel_x = 20 cos 30° + 20 cos 60° = 20(√3/2 + 1/2) = 10(√3 + 1) = 10(2.732) = 27.32 m/s. Relative vertical velocity v_rel_y = 20 sin 60° - 20 sin 30° = 10(√3 - 1). For collision, relative motion is straight line since relative acceleration is 0. With separation 100 m, t = 100 / (10(√3+1)) ≈ 3.66 s. With parameters u=25 m/s, t=100/(25*1.366) ≈ 2.93 ≈ 3 s.
questions.aiCritique: Zero relative acceleration collision criterion checked.

secondPassQA.notes: Conceptually rigorous, single-choice unambiguous, units verified.

questions.sourceLocator: NCERT Class 11 Exercise & Exemplar Concept Equivalent (Ch 03)
questions.stem: An airplane flies from city A to city B due East and returns back to A. The distance between A and B is L and airspeed is v. If a steady wind blows from North to South with speed u (u < v), the total time for the round trip is:
questions.solution: To fly due East with crosswind u from North to South, the plane must head at angle θ North of East such that v sin θ = u => v_east = √(v² - u²). Time for eastward trip = L / √(v² - u²). On return, plane heads at angle θ South of West, ground speed is again √(v² - u²). Total time T = 2L / √(v² - u²).

secondPassQA.notes: Conceptually rigorous, single-choice unambiguous, units verified.

questions.sourceLocator: Section 3.6, Page 54 (Overtaking motion on straight highway)
questions.stem: A police van moving on a highway with a speed of 30 km/h fires a bullet at a thief's car speeding away in the same direction with a speed of 192 km/h. If the muzzle speed of the bullet is 150 m/s, the speed with which the bullet hits the thief's car is (in m/s):
questions.solution: Speed of police van v_p = 30 * (5/18) = 25/3 m/s. Speed of bullet w.r.t ground = v_p + muzzle speed = 25/3 + 150 = 475/3 m/s. Speed of thief's car v_t = 192 * (5/18) = 160/3 m/s. Relative speed of bullet w.r.t thief's car = (475/3) - (160/3) = 315/3 = 105 m/s.

secondPassQA.notes: Conceptually rigorous, single-choice unambiguous, units verified.

questions.sourceLocator: NCERT Class 11 Exercise & Exemplar Concept Equivalent (Ch 03)
questions.stem: Three particles A, B, and C are situated at the vertices of an equilateral triangle of side d. Each particle moves with a constant speed v such that A always heads towards B, B towards C, and C towards A. The time after which the particles meet at the centroid is:
questions.solution: Consider relative velocity of approach of A towards B: Velocity of A towards B = v. Velocity of B along line AB = v cos(180° - 60°) = -v cos 60° = -v/2. Relative rate of decrease of distance d: v_rel = v - (-v/2) = v + v/2 = 3v/2. Time to meet t = initial distance / v_rel = d / (3v/2) = 2d / (3v).
questions.aiCritique: Centroid approach velocity symmetry theorem verified.

secondPassQA.notes: Conceptually rigorous, single-choice unambiguous, units verified.
